title: W.P No. 187-B of 2026 Syed Muhammad  Vs  Khan Bahadur alias Fazal-ur-Rehman, etc
text:
IN THE PESHAWAR HIGH COT]RT,
BANNU BENCH

Syed Muhammad
Vs
Khan Bahadur alias Fazal-ur-Rehman, etc'
JUDGMENT
Date of hearing: 01.06.2026
For petitioner(s): Mr, Rizwan Ullah Wazir Advocat

MUHAMMAD TARIO AFRID J.- This writ petition, filed
under Article 199 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of
Pakistan, 1973, calls in question the legality and validity ofthe
judgment and order dated 17.02.2026 passed by the leamed
Additional District Judge-V, Bannu, whereby the civil revision
preferred by the petitioner was dismissed, and the order dated
28.10.2024 passed by the leamed Civil Judge-XIII' Bannu'
returning the plaint under Order VII, Rule 10 CPC for its
presentation before the Coun of competent jurisdiction' was
maintained.
2. Briefly stated, the facts ofthe case leading to the filing of
this writ petition are that plaintiff, Syed Muhammad (hereinafter
referred to as the petitioner), instituted a suit for declaration and
permanent mandatory injunction against defendants' Khan
Bahadur and others (hereinafter referred to as the respondents)'
contending that suit Plot No'1779, measuring 05 marlas' situated
in Jalozai Housing Scheme, Tehsil Pabbi' District Nowshera' was
originally allotted to one Aman Ullah Khan vide allotment letter
by
dated 18.06.2013, and was subsequently purchased the
petitioner through a sale deed dated 13'08'2013' It was averred
(S.8.) Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Tariq Afridi
@hafoor Zaman)
-2-
that respondent No.2, Nasib Noor' who is the brother of the
petitioner and was jointly engaged in property business with
respondent No.l , obtained the original documents of the plot from
the petitioner and handed them over to respondent No' 1 to be used
as security in arbitration proceedings arising out of a business
dispute between respondents No.l and 2' Later on, both
respondents claimed that the documents had gone missing,
constraining the petitioner to issue a public notice in daily 'Ausaf
it
dated 14.06.2020 regarding their loss' Subsequently' was
discovered that through arbitration proceedings dated 21'09'2020'
2
25.09.2020, ail 29.09.2020, respondents No'1 and had
transferred the suit plot to respondent No'3 without his
?
knowledge, authority or consent' Consequently, the petitioner
instituted the suit seeking declaration that the impugned acts were
illegal, void ab initio, and ineffective upon his rights' along with
cancellation of all subsequent transactions flowing therefrom'
3. Upon appearance, respondent No' 3 contested the claim of
the petitioner by filing a written statement, wherein various legal
and factual objections were raised' She also filed an application
under Order VII, Rule 1l CPC seeking rejection of the plaint on
of
three grounds. Firstly, it was contended that the subject matter
the suit, namely the plot in question, is situated in Jalozai Housing
Scheme at Tehsil Pabbi, District Nowshera' Secondly' the
transaction relating to the transfer of the suit plot in favour of
respondent No' 3 also took place at Peshawar' Thirdly' respondent
No. 4, namely the Provincial Housing Authority GHA)' is
likewise located at Peshawar' On the basis of these facts' the
respondent No. 3 asserted that the Trial Court at Bannu lacked
territorial jurisdiction to entertain the suit and' therefore' the plaint
was liable to be rejected.
4, Contrarily, the petitioner filed a replication to the said
application and contended that the execution of sale deed dated
(S.B.) Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Tariq Afridi
(Ghafoor Zaman)
-3 -
13.08.2013 and payment ofthe sale consideration had taken place
at Dishict Bannu. It was further asserted that the arbitration
proceedings culminating into decisions dated 2l-09.2020,
26.09.2020, and 29.09.2020, were also conducted and reduced
into writing at District Bannu. The petitioner also contended that
Aman Ullah Khan, the original owner / allottee with whom the
sale deed dated 13.08.2013 was executed, is also a resident of
District Bannu. On the strength of these facts, the petitioner
contended that part of the cause of action had arisen within the
territorial limits of District Bannu and, therefore, the Trial Court
at Bannu was well within its jurisdiction to entertain and
adjudicate the lis.
5. After hearing the arguments and examining the material
available on record, the Trial Court came to the conclusion that it
had no jurisdiction to entertain and adjudicate upon the matter'
Consequently, vide order dated 28.10'2024, the plaint was
retumed under ORDER VII Rule 10 CPC for presentation before
the Court of competent jurisdiction. Feeling aggrieved, the
petitioner preferred a civil revision before the leamed Additional
it
District Judge-V, Bannu; however, was dismissed vide
judgment and order dated 17.02.2026.Hence, this petition'
6.
Arguments heard. Record perused.
7. Admittedly, the suit property is situated \nlalozai Housing
Scheme at Tehsil Pabbi, District Nowshera' Section 16 CPC
provides that suits for recovery of immovable property or
determinationofanyrightorinterestthereinshallbeinstifutedin
the Court within whose local territorial jurisdiction such property
is situated. The scheme of the provision leaves no room for
conffoversy that in matters concerning immovable property'
jurisdiction is to be determined with reference to the situs of the
property. A Court outside those territorial limits cannot assume
jurisdiction merely on the basis of ancillary facts, when the
(Ghafoor Zaman) (S.8.) llon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad 'Iariq Afridi
-4-
principal controversy relates to recovery or determination of any
right or interest in immovable propefty.
8. ail
A conjoint reading of Sections 16 20 CPC reveals that
where the dispute pertains to any right or interest in immovable
property, the special provision of Section 16 CPC prevails, and
the suit is to be instituted before the Court within whose territorial
jurisdiction the property is situated. Section 20 CPC, being
general in nature, cannot override the mandate of Section 16 CPC.
In the present case, the owner resides in District Peshawar, the
suit property is situated in Jalozai Housing Scheme at Tehsil
Pabbi, District Nowshera, and the office of the Provincial Housing
Authority, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa situated at Peshawar maintains
the official record pertaining to allotment and transfer of plots,
including the disputed plot situated at Jalozai Housing Scheme.
The alleged fraudulent act of defendant No.l, who is merely the
petitioner's brother, resident of District Bannu, and not owner of
the property, does not create any cause of action under Section
20(c) CPC nor confer jurisdiction upon the Court at Bannu. Since
the controversy essentially relates to rights in immovable
property, only the Court within whose teritorial limits the
property is situated has jurisdiction to adjudicate the matter.
g. Leamed counsel for the petitioner laid considerable
emphasis upon the alleged execution of the sale deed dated
13.08.2013, payment of sale consideration, and subsequent
arbitration proceedings, all allegedly took place at Bannu;
however, in view of the foregoing, these events do not advance
the petitioner's case for the simple reason that the claim
substantially relates to rights and interests in immovable property
situated at Tehsil Pabbi, District Nowshera.
In Haii Abdul Malik and l0 othe rs v. Muhammad
10.
Anwar Khan a nd 26 others (2003 SCMR 990), the august
Supreme Court of Pakistan held that where a suit involves a
(Ghafoor Zaman) (S.s.) Hon'ble N4r. Justice Muhammad Tariq Afridi
5
dispute relating to rights or interests in immovable property, it is
maintainable only before the Court within whose territorial
jurisdiction the property is situated. It was further held that where
the relief claimed does not relate to any right or interest in the
property and is confined to an ancillary matter, the suit may be
instituted at a place where the cause of action wholly or partly
arose.
11. In these circumstances, the leamed Trial Court rightly
retumed the plaint under Order VII' Rule 10 CPC for presentation
before the Court of competent jurisdiction, and the said order was
correctly upheld by the impugned judgment. Both the Courts
below have recorded findings which are in accordance with the
settled principles goveming territorial jurisdiction in suits relating
to immovable property. The jurisdiction of this Court under
Article 199 of the Constitution is not meant to re-examine
findings which are otherwise in accordance with law unless the
impugned orders are shown to suffer from a jurisdictional defect'
illegality, or material irregularity. No such infirmity has been
pointed out in the Present case'
12. Consequently, finding no ground warranting interference in
constitutional jurisdiction, this petition is dismissed in limine'
However, it is clarified that the petitioner shall be at liberty to
approach the competent Court at District Peshawar or District
Nowshera, as the case may be, for presentation of the plaint, after
its retum by the leamed Trial Court at Bannu, in accordance with
law.

headnote:
Writ Petition Held: Constitution of Pakistan, 1973---Article 199---Code of Civil Procedure, 1908---Sections 16 & 20---
Order VII, Rule 10---Territorial jurisdiction---Return of plaint---Dispute relating to immovable property---
Determination of rights and interests in property---Scope---Petitioner instituted a civil suit before the Civil
Court at Bannu, seeking declaration, cancellation of transactions and permanent mandatory injunction in
respect of Plot No.1779 situated in Jalozai Housing Scheme at Tehsil Pabbi, District Nowshera, alleging that the property had been fraudulently transferred without his consent through arbitration proceedings conducted by the respondents---Defendant questioned maintainability of suit on the ground that the property was situated in District Nowshera, the transfer transaction had taken place at Peshawar, and the record was maintained by the Provincial Housing Authority at Peshawar---Trial Court returned the plaint under Order VII, Rule 10 CPC for presentation before the Court of competent jurisdiction, which order was maintained in revision---Petitioner contended that the sale deed, payment of consideration, and arbitration proceedings culminating in fraudulent transfer of the suit plot had taken place at Bannu and, therefore, part of the cause of action had arisen within the territorial jurisdiction of Trial Court at Bannu---Held, a conjoint reading of Sections 16 and 20 CPC reveals that where the dispute pertains to determination of rights or interests in immovable property, the special provisions of Section 16 CPC would govern the matter and jurisdiction is to be determined with reference to the situs of the property, while Section 20 CPC, being a general provision, cannot override the mandate of Section 16 CPC---Record revealed that contesting defendant resided at Peshawar, while the Provincial Housing Authority, which maintained the official record pertaining to the allotment and transfer of plots, including the disputed plot, was situated at Peshawar, whereas the suit property was situated in Jalozai Housing Scheme at Tehsil Pabbi, District Nowshera---Ancillary facts, such as the alleged execution of documents, payment of consideration, or conduct of arbitration proceedings, do not confer territorial jurisdiction upon the Trial Court at Bannu when the principal controversy relates to immovable property situated beyond its territorial limits---Only the Court within whose local jurisdiction the property is situated is competent to entertain and adjudicate such dispute---Alleged fraudulent acts of one of the defendants residing at Bannu do not create a cause of action under Section 20(c) CPC so as to confer jurisdiction upon the Civil Court at Bannu---Findings recorded by the Courts below were in accordance with settled principles of law and suffered from no jurisdictional defect, illegality or material irregularity warranting interference in constitutional jurisdiction---Petition dismissed in limine with liberty to the petitioner to present the plaint before the Court of competent jurisdiction at District Peshawar or District Nowshera, as the case may be, in accordance with law.
